generic_method.input: Original public Movebank released event-level CSV, not a review of authors' summary results
generic_method.sensor: row sensor-type gps; visible=true, georeferenced, valid animal/time
generic_method.animal_day_weights: Each unique UTC date has equal total weight per animal; original fixes on same date weighted equally
generic_method.projection: equirectangular x=lon*111.32*cos(mean valid source latitude), y=lat*111.32; all grid coordinates aggregate only
generic_method.grid_shift_sensitivity: zero and half-width offsets in 2D for source-specific verified turtle cohort
generic_method.dependency: pair_month observations heavily reuse same animals; no treating dyads, months or records as independent

results.label: wolf
results.interpretation: Most pairs in this source have negligible direct estimated monthly 5–20 km XY utilization overlap. Pack/cohort access and territorial resource opportunity not yet authenticated; cannot claim within-population competition or individual behavior partitions.

results.label: elephant
results.reference_population: Fourteen female elephants from 14 separate herds in Kruger National Park per source paper; shared park not a shared accessible foraging territory
results.interpretation: Estimated landscape-level shared 2D utilization varies among herd representatives. Separate herds and source access/history create primary confounds. Paper already demonstrated water/temperature movement strategies; those prior findings are not novel products of this analysis.

results.label: green_turtle
results.source_population: Diego Garcia nesting female green turtles tracked in 2012, 2015, 2017 and 2018; split tagging cohorts and biological movement stages
results.source_note: 2018 comparison retains same 12 adults in Jul and Nov, so 66 pair contrasts are not independent
results.interpretation: Within SAME tracking adults from a shared nesting area, monthly XY use converges early then diverges while turtles move to different foraging regions. This is stage/calendar-driven, NOT evidence of persistent individual movement policy or diet separation; postnesting dispersal and different home ranges were published by original authors.

sensor_exclusions.label: Canadian herring gull
sensor_exclusions.reason: Not true original GPS; leave out of high precision XY identity primary tier (Argos measurement-model stratum only)

sensor_exclusions.label: Galapagos tortoise monthly supplementary
sensor_exclusions.reason: This released table holds original-paper monthly movement metrics, not time-stamped raw GPS fixes; refrain from treating its rows as independent tracks

limits: These are retrospective exploratory source comparisons not prospective tests or a new universal ecological finding
Fixed-grid/finite sampling and broad common-park or shared-nesting-site opportunity must not be equated to resources or realized encounters
Strong turtle onset-versus-distribution contrast recapitulates well documented nest→foraging dispersal, and cannot establish repeated individual specialization without re-exposure
Wolf and elephant mostly unshared sampled places: conditional same-place behavioral identity R needs a separate common-place gate; it is NOT measured here
No independently measured prey/food/resource overlap, synchronized physical encounters, causal mechanism, or multilevel 3-clade meta-regression has been calculated
Source original location data never copied into this repository; download authorized public data under source rights for a reproducibility rerun
